Summary

Pre-registered verdict: this is the full-data run, judged by the criteria in analysis/prereg_mvp1.md and analysis/prereg_mvp2.md.

Asks: the question each analysis answers, in one line each.

QuestionAnswer
Q3: how are price, trade size and wallet volume distributed?Descriptive, no pre-registered criterion. Median trade size 6.93 USDC, mean 129.8 USDC. Closest of the three fits for trade size: power law (KS D 0.03883). Mean price p_1d 0.3757.
Q1: do prices match how often events happen?Prices are not calibrated as a whole at this n. chi-square 67.99 (df 10), p < 0.0001, Cohen's w 0.03766, n 47,948. bins off bh 5, bins off bonferroni 4, brier 0.1071.
Q2: is wallet volume concentrated?Descriptive, no pre-registered criterion. Gini maker 0.978, taker 0.9625. The top 1% of maker wallets hold 86.1% of maker volume. A wallet is an address, not a person.
Q1a: does accuracy depend on the topic?Accuracy depends on the topic at this n. chi-square 3,204 (df 7), p < 0.0001, Cramer's V 0.2585, n 47,948. n categories 8.
Q1b: is the price better near the deadline?Better near the deadline. t 19.96 (df 11004), p < 0.0001, Cohen's d 0.1903, mean difference 0.0257, 95% CI [0.02318, 0.02822], n 11,005.
Q1c: are busier markets more accurate?No evidence that busier markets are more accurate at this n. Spearman rho 0.226, p < 0.0001, rho 0.226, 95% CI [0.2173, 0.2348], n 47,948.

Table 1. Questions and answers. Verdicts come from verdicts.json, numbers from the saved results.

How to read

  • Each answer repeats numbers from the sections below. Check the p-value together with the effect size.
  • With tens of thousands of markets, a small effect can give a tiny p. Read the effect size first.
  • Tests assume independent markets. Markets on one event are not independent.

How to read

  • A smaller KS D means a closer fit. D is the size of the gap, p only says if the gap is zero.
  • KS p-values are optimistic for fitted parameters. The fit used the same data as the test.
  • Mean far above median means a long right tail: a few large trades and wallets.
  • Wallet volume pools maker and taker rows, so one address can appear twice.

How to read

  • Pre-registered line: chi-square p < 0.05 means prices are not calibrated as a whole.
  • A bin is off when its BH-corrected p < 0.05. A negative difference means the event happened less often than priced.
  • Effect w is Cohen's w. About 0.1 is small. A tiny p with a small w is a real but small gap.
  • Brier is the mean squared error of the price. 0.25 is a coin flip at 0.5, 0 is perfect.

Step 10 of 10

Method notes and reproduce

Method notes and limits

  • KS p-values are optimistic when parameters are fitted to the same data.
  • K-means is a side analysis. The clusters describe the sample.
  • A wallet is an address, not a person.
  • Tests assume independent markets. Markets on one event are not independent.
  • Duplicate rows are kept. Volume includes trades after T - 1 day.
  • Q1b uses 11,005 of 47,948 kept markets (23.0%). These are long, active markets, so the Q1b answer is about them.
  • Q1c: Brier error is larger for contested markets (price near 0.5) by construction. So rho (0.226) mixes activity with how contested the market is.
  • Q1 covers only markets with a trade at least 1 day before T. 215,289 markets (31.3% of scope) have none and are dropped (no_price).
  • no_outcome (62,718 markets) includes markets whose outcome_seq=1 label never traded.
  • Pre-registered verdicts exist only for scope = full runs. Sports n in Q1a: Sports 19,162.
